claims.text: FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles can be prepared as well-mixed, near-equiatomic solid solutions.
Well-tempered metadynamics or umbrella sampling can compute free-energy profiles for FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles as functions of temperature and particle size.
The relevant free-energy landscape can be represented using collective variables such as structural order parameters or surface-to-volume ratios.
Free-energy barriers govern the thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
Enhanced-sampling methods facilitate observation of rare events and transitions that standard molecular dynamics may miss.
Thermal transitions in high-entropy alloy nanoparticles may include phase separation, melting, and morphological or chemical restructuring.
Enhanced sampling can accurately map barriers associated with thermal destabilization.
Thermal-destabilization barriers vary with FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticle size.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles will have lower free-energy barriers to thermal transitions.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles will undergo earlier or more pronounced thermal transitions.
Larger FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles will have higher free-energy barriers and greater thermal stability.
Enhanced sampling will resolve size dependence more clearly than standard molecular dynamics alone.
Standard molecular dynamics with empirical potentials typically undersamples rare events.
Standard molecular dynamics fails to rigorously capture the size-dependent free-energy landscape.
The quantitative size dependence of free-energy barriers and transition temperatures remains unknown until simulations are performed.
The choice of collective variables and metadynamics parameters may affect the simulation results.
